title: Exact-v6 iterative neural regret pilot
benchmark: A frozen learned policy plays at least 100,000 fresh 200bb HUNL Slumbot hands, scores above 0 bb/100, and has a 95% confidence-interval lower bound above 0.
hypothesis: With the selected 128-step dose and live-feature passive initialization, three exact-v6 regret iterations will remain computationally bounded, preserve resumable evidence, and produce a terminal policy whose fixed-panel greedy average improves over initialization on at least two of three generic anchors.
material_change: Run three iterations with two root traversals per player, fresh-Adam 128-step updates matching the dose control, per-iteration network/buffer/RNG/strategy snapshots, and terminal-only interpretation on a fixed 128-pair call-station/uniform/min-bet sampled+greedy panel.
baseline: The matched dose control selected 128 steps after 35.2%/33.5% held-out loss reductions; no iterative performance evidence exists yet.
notes: Terminal iteration is frozen before evaluation and is the only candidate used for admission; intermediate evaluations form a learning-curve diagnostic, not checkpoint selection.

result.summary: Three exact-v6 iterations completed and reloaded exactly, but terminal greedy generic-anchor mean declined from +69.26 to -359.11 bb/100 and only one of three anchors improved. Traverser-node counts became sharply seat-asymmetric under within-iteration sequential updates.
result.conclusion: The selected optimizer dose creates large behavior change but the sequential collect-update ordering is confounded and the resulting terminal curve is not promising. Larger training is rejected until iteration synchronization is tested.
result.next_step: Run a same-budget matched synchronization control: freeze both networks at iteration start, collect both traversers on common decks, then update both; compare sample imbalance and terminal fixed-panel curve against this sequential treatment.
